title: Lawrence Welk and the "Primrose Lane" theme for The Smith Family
summary: Callender defends Welk, and tells how his one pop hit became a TV theme and how its royalties helped after the Sylmar earthquake.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: I was on that, too. No, Lawrence Welk I guess a lot of people don't understand. But what's wrong with Lawrence Welk? I like him. He plays the melody. And also, at least once or twice a year, he writes a tune I wrote, my only Pop hit tune, "Primrose Lane." So every time I would see him, he'd say, "Hey, I played your tune."
It was nice. It's really helped my ASCAP because "Primrose Lane" was used on The Smith Family, Henry

Ponda's show. Do you remember that? He played a policeman, and they happened to live on Primrose Lane. So the opening shot was of Primrose Lane, and they played my song which was named "Primrose Lane" as the theme of the show. And the funny way that happened, I had a call from Frank de Vol. He said, "You've got to go do this date with me." I said, "Of course!" I liked working with him anyhow. He's one of the nice people I know. Out of the many nice people, he's one of the very nicest. Anyhow, I get in the studio, and I open the music up, and here's "Primrose Lane." I said, "Hey, what's going on?" He said, "Well, they're using your song as the theme, and I thought I'd surprise you by calling you to do the date."

Yeah, I thought so. And that's the period when we had the big earthquake, and we were in Sylmar. I got completely wiped out. So on the strength of "Primrose Lane," Ella Fitzgerald was doing it, the Mills Brothers were doing it, Pearl Bailey was doing it on her show... And on the strength of that, I called up ASCAP and said, "I need some money right away." They said, "Well, what do you need?" So I said, "I need five thousand dollars in a hurry." And the second day after that, the check was in the mail. So thank God for hit records. They help.
